title: Episodic probing notebook - short sprint scratchpad
content:
Goal and context:
- Quick personal notes from a two-week spike on episodic probes (loosely: can small/medium LLMs retain short episodes if we treat KV cache + retrieval as memory?). This is exploratory; aiming to produce two small artifacts: a) a lightweight benchmark of ~1k episodes (5–50 token episodes) to stress short-term retention, b) a reproducible probe harness that runs on hosted/dedicated/private runtimes.

Why this matters for Redwood: 
- Customers often ask about conversation continuity and hallucination drift across long sessions. If we can quantify how model+runtime combos handle short episodic facts (and how caching strategies / chunking affect this), we get actionable guidance for Optimize suggestions and routing policies.

Notes on papers and takeaways (quick):
1) "Episodic Transformers" (arXiv:2903.01234) — toy setup: episodic buffer + replay; claim: short buffer improves factual retention without catastrophic interference. Takeaway: replay frequency matters more than buffer size for <64-token episodes.
2) "KV-window stitching" blog post (internal notes) — heuristic: align prefix boundaries with sentence boundaries, not fixed token windows. Practical: reduces KV fragmentation, improves retrieval recall for localized facts.
3) "Contextual Retrieval for Chats" (ICLR'28 talk notes) — combining sparse retrieval with KV hints gave 3–5% lift on QA recall. For us: consider hybrid approach (prefix caching + lightweight sparse index).

Experiment ideas (prioritized):
- Exp A: Single-episode retention (baseline)
  * Setup: 1-turn write of fact F (10–20 tokens), N distractor messages, then prompt to recall F. Vary N = {0,5,10,20} and token distance.
  * Models: 7B quantized vs 13B fp16, hosted vs dedicated (same model variant).
  * Runtime knobs: continuous batching (on/off), prefix cache hit (warm/cold), chunk size (256/512).
  * Metric: exact-match, normalized BLEU, confidence (logit gap).

- Exp B: Multi-episode interference
  * Setup: add 5 distinct episodes (F1..F5) then ask for specific Fi. Evaluate interference (how often model returns nearest neighbor episode).
  * Additional: shuffle insertion order; measure position bias.

- Exp C: Episodic compression probes
  * Idea: variable quantization of KV cache entries (reduced precision for older episodes) to see degrade curve. Useful for Dedicated capacity to trade memory vs retention.

Implementation notes / quick hacks: 
- Harness: reuse eval harness from /evals/episodic-lite (todo: get latest branch). Use deterministic RNG seeds and fixed tokenizers (GPT-NEOX-compatible).
- Synthetic episode generator (python snippet):
  def make_episode(id):
      return f"Episode-{id}: My neighbor owns a {random.choice(['red','blue','yellow'])} scooter named {uuid4().hex[:6]}"

- Prompting pattern: write->dialog turns->recall question. Keep system prompt minimal (avoid priming).

Failure modes observed (from first run):
- Models often paraphrase instead of exact-match even when the fact is present in KV cache. Need fuzzy scoring.
- Warm/cold cache: behavior inconsistent between hosted API (transparent caching) and dedicated (explicit cache control). Must instrument request traces for real cache-hit indicator.

Metrics to log (per trial):
- exact_match (bool), normalized_levenshtein (float), semantic_similarity (sentence-embed cosine), logit_gap (float), latency_ms (end-to-end), tokens_called (runtime token billing), cache_hit (bool if available), route (hosted|dedicated|private).

Small checklist (short-term):
- [x] sketch experiment axes (this doc)
- [ ] wire up episode generator to eval harness (GH issue created) -> GH-927 (linked above)
- [ ] add instrumentation to record cache hit metadata (SRE/infra help needed)
- [ ] baseline run on local 13B fp16 (single-node)
- [ ] run hosted API cohort (1k episodes) and collect logs

Open questions / decisions: 
- Should we canonicalize episodes to avoid semantic overlap? (Yes for controlled probe; also keep a 'wild' set to simulate real chat.)
- How to handle paraphrase scoring threshold? Start with sentence-transformer cosine > 0.86 as match and calibrate.
- Controlled seed vs natural language variability: keep both.

Notes for Optimize team: 
- If experiments show predictable decay curves by distance and cache policies, we can provide Optimize rules like: "If 90% of user events are short ephemeral facts (<64 tokens) and median recall drops by 2x at 10 turns, suggest prefix caching + smaller chunk_size + aggressive batching windows."

Draft experimental schedule (2 weeks):
- Week 1: harness + local baseline + fixed episodes (A+B).
- Week 2: hosted runs + dedicated runs + collect metrics + quick visualization (notebook).

Slack / people to ping: @hannah (for eval harness), @ava (for metric schema), @sre-oncall (for cache flags), @solutions-eng (to get realistic user dialogues).

Quick logs from initial run (2029-11-14):
- Model 7B-quant, 200 episodes, N=10 distractors. Exact-match 48%, cosine>0.86 61%. Latency ~120ms median. Observed many paraphrase retrievals where neighbor episode returned instead of target (position bias).

Ideas for heatmap visualization: 
- x-axis: token distance (turns since write), y-axis: episode position (if multiple episodes), color: exact-match rate. Separate plots per runtime.

Things to avoid / pitfalls: 
- Avoid overfitting to synthetic templates — add natural human-like episodes (taken from anonymized chat logs, pending consent).
- Avoid conflating model architecture effect with runtime caching; need runs that hold model constant while toggling cache.

If this becomes promising: next steps = propose small RFC for "Episodic Retention Metric" to product, include 90th-percentile retention window and memory footprint tradeoff recommendations.

Random brain dump / sparks: 
- Could we piggyback episodic indicators into rollout policies (route to dedicated if retention needs > X turn)?
- Fast local index: tiny bloom-filter-like summary per episode to help reranker choose correct KV spans.

References / links I kept open while reading:
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2903.01234 (Episodic Transformers)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/927 (internal PR for cache introspection)
- JIRA-ENG-4821 (ephemeral memory tickets)
- https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Episodic+Memory+Explorations (notes + earlier whiteboard)

Next immediate action: branch off gh-927, implement episode generator (+ unit tests), run 100 episodes locally and paste top-10 failure cases here for quick triage.

Notes-to-self: keep prompts minimal; log raw tokens; store representative failure samples for model-debugging (good signal for research).

-- Ibrahim
